hook_1.message: Take a look at these two bars. Something is the same, and something is different.

hook_2.message: What do you notice about the colored parts?

options.label: They take up the same space

hook_redirect.message: Good observation! They do look different. But try looking at just the colored parts. Do they stop at the same spot?

hook_retry.message: Do the colored parts take up the same amount of space?

options.label: I still do not see it

hook_give.message: That is totally okay! The colored parts do end at the same spot. One bar has more pieces, but the colored amount is the same.

hook_confirm.message: That is right! Great eye. Different number of pieces, but the colored part is the same size.

define_1.message: When two fractions look different but show the same amount, we call them equivalent fractions.

define_2.message: 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent fractions. Different numbers, same amount colored. Let's find out how that works!

shade_wait.message: Here is one whole bar with nothing colored yet. Tap it to color it in!
shade_wait.hint: Just tap once on the bar!

shade_confirm.message: Nice work! You colored the whole bar. That is 1 out of 1 piece colored.

cut_intro.message: Now I am going to cut this bar into 2 equal pieces. Watch what happens.

cut_observe.message: I cut the bar, but the colored amount did not change. There are 2 pieces now, and 1 of them is colored.

cut_question.message: If there are 2 pieces and 1 is colored, how do we write that as a fraction?

cut_redirect.message: Good try! The total pieces go on the bottom. The colored pieces go on the top. There are 2 total and 1 colored.

cut_retry.message: 1 colored piece on top, 2 total pieces on the bottom. What fraction is that?

cut_give.message: No worries! That is 1/2. The colored piece is 1, and the total is 2. So we write 1 on top and 2 on the bottom.

cut_confirm.message: That is right! 1 out of 2 pieces is colored. We write that as 1/2. Well done!

build_bridge.message: Here is the big idea. If we cut a bar into more pieces, we can find a new fraction that shows the same amount!

split_wait.message: I added a blue bar below. You can cut a piece by tapping it two times quickly. Try it on the blue bar!
split_wait.hint: Tap the same piece two times quickly!

equiv_wait_1.message: Great job! One piece became two. Now keep cutting the blue bar until you have 4 pieces, then tap 2 of them to color them.
equiv_wait_1.hint: Double-tap to cut pieces. Single-tap to color them.

equiv_reveal_1.message: Wonderful! Look at both bars. The colored parts end at the same spot. The bottom bar has smaller pieces, but the colored amount is the same!

equiv_question_1.message: 1/2 and 2/4. Do they show the same amount of color?

equiv_redirect_1.message: I can see why you think that! The numbers are bigger. But look at the bars. The smaller pieces take up the same total space.

equiv_retry_1.message: Do the colored parts on the two bars end at the same spot?

equiv_give_1.message: That is okay! They do line up. The colored parts are the same size, so 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent fractions.

equiv_confirm_1.message: That is right! 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent fractions. You are doing a great job!

equiv_more_setup.message: Can we find even more fractions equivalent to 1/2? Look — here is 1/2 on top, your 2/4 in the middle, and now 3/6 at the bottom.

equiv_more_question.message: 1/2, 2/4, and 3/6. Do all three colored parts line up?

equiv_more_redirect.message: No problem! Look at the right edge of each colored part. All three stop at the exact same place.

equiv_more_retry.message: The color stops at the same place on all three bars. Does that mean 1/2, 2/4, and 3/6 are equivalent?

equiv_more_give.message: They are! When the colored parts take up the same space, the fractions are equivalent. You are learning fast!

equiv_more_confirm.message: That is right! 1/2, 2/4, and 3/6 all show the same amount. Great work finding all of those!

pattern_question.message: Every time we cut into more pieces, the pieces get smaller but we color more. What happens to the total colored amount?

pattern_redirect.message: Good thinking! But look at the bars again. More colored pieces, but each one is smaller. The total colored space has not changed.

pattern_retry.message: Smaller pieces, but more of them colored. Does the colored amount stay the same or change?

pattern_give.message: It stays the same! Cutting makes smaller pieces, but you color more of them. That is how equivalent fractions work!

pattern_confirm.message: Exactly! The colored amount stays the same. That is the secret to equivalent fractions. Now let's try a different one!

challenge_2_wait.message: This time the top bar shows 2/3. Cut and color the purple bar below until the colored parts match the top bar.
challenge_2_wait.hint: Try cutting into 6 pieces and coloring 4. See if the colored parts line up!

challenge_2_reveal.message: Well done! The colored parts line up. You found a fraction equivalent to 2/3!

challenge_2_question.message: You cut each piece in half and colored twice as many. Did the colored amount change?

challenge_2_redirect.message: I see why you might think that! But look at the bars. The colored parts end at the same spot. The total colored amount has not changed.

challenge_2_retry.message: If the colored parts are the same size, are the fractions equivalent?

challenge_2_give.message: They are equivalent! The colored parts are the same size. You are doing really well!

challenge_2_confirm.message: That is right! The colored amount stayed the same. You are getting really good at this!

non_example_setup.message: Now here is an important question. Are all fractions equivalent? Let's look at these two bars.

non_example_question.message: The top shows 1/2 and the bottom shows 1/3. Do the colored parts end at the same spot?

non_example_redirect.message: Good try! Look carefully at where the color ends. The teal bar has more color than the coral bar.

non_example_retry.message: Which bar has a bigger colored part?

non_example_give.message: No worries! 3 is a bigger number, but more pieces means each piece is smaller. So 1 out of 3 is less than 1 out of 2.

non_example_correct.message: That is right! The colored parts do not line up. That means 1/2 and 1/3 are not equivalent.

non_example_why.message: If the colored parts do not match, the fractions are not equivalent. The bars always tell the truth!

circle_intro.message: You have been using bars to find equivalent fractions. But does it work with other shapes too? Let's try circles!

circle_half_setup.message: Here is a circle cut into 2 equal parts, with 1 part colored. That is 1/2.

circle_quarter_setup.message: Now here is the same circle cut into 4 equal parts, with 2 parts colored. That is 2/4.

circle_half_question.message: Look at the colored parts of both circles. Is the same amount colored in each one?

circle_half_redirect.message: Good observation! The pieces look different because one circle has more slices. But look at the total colored area on each circle.

circle_half_retry.message: Does the colored area cover the same amount of each circle?

circle_half_give.message: It does! Half the circle is colored in both. 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent, just like we saw with the bars!

circle_half_confirm.message: That is right! Half of each circle is colored. 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent. It works with circles too!

circle_thirds_setup.message: Let's try another one. Here is a circle showing 2/3, and another showing 4/6.

circle_thirds_question.message: Is the same amount of each circle colored?

circle_thirds_redirect.message: Look at how much of each circle is colored. The second circle has more slices, but each slice is smaller.

circle_thirds_retry.message: Smaller slices, but more of them colored. Is the total colored amount the same?

circle_thirds_give.message: It is the same! 2/3 and 4/6 both have the same area colored. Equivalent fractions work with any shape!

circle_thirds_confirm.message: That is right! 2/3 and 4/6 are equivalent. The same idea works whether we use bars or circles. Great job!

circle_nonexample_setup.message: Now let's check one that does not match. Here is 1/2 and 1/3 as circles.

circle_nonexample_question.message: Is the same amount colored in each circle?

circle_nonexample_redirect.message: Look again! The first circle has half its area colored. The second circle has only a third colored. That is less!

circle_nonexample_retry.message: Half of a circle is bigger than a third of a circle. Are they equivalent?

circle_nonexample_give.message: They are not equivalent! 1/2 has more area colored than 1/3. It works the same as with bars.

circle_nonexample_correct.message: That is right! 1/2 and 1/3 are not equivalent. The colored areas are different sizes, just like with the bars!

circle_summary.message: Whether we use bars or circles, the rule is the same. If the colored amount is the same, the fractions are equivalent!

play_intro.message: Now it is your turn to play! You are going to build your own fractions and see if you can make them match.

play_add_bar_teach.message: First, let's add a bar. Tap the empty space twice to create a new one!

play_add_bar_wait.message: Tap the empty space twice to add a bar.
play_add_bar_wait.hint: Double-tap the open area below to make a new bar!

play_add_bar_confirm.message: There it is! You made a brand new bar. Now cut it and color it to build 1/2.

play_build_half_wait.message: Cut the bar into 2 pieces and color 1 of them to make 1/2.
play_build_half_wait.hint: Double-tap to cut, then single-tap one piece to color it!

play_build_half_confirm.message: You built 1/2 all by yourself! Now here is the challenge. Add another bar and build a fraction equivalent to 1/2.

play_add_equiv_wait.message: Tap the empty space twice to add a second bar.
play_add_equiv_wait.hint: Double-tap the open area to add another bar!

play_build_equiv_instruct.message: Great! Now cut and color this new bar to make it equivalent to 1/2. It could be 2/4, 3/6, or anything that matches!

play_build_equiv_wait.message: Build a fraction equivalent to 1/2 on the second bar.
play_build_equiv_wait.hint: Try 2/4! Cut into 4 pieces and color 2 of them.

play_equiv_celebrate.message: Look at that! The colored parts line up. You built two equivalent fractions all on your own! Wonderful job!

play_smash_teach.message: Now let's learn one more move. You can smash a bar to get rid of it. Hold down on a bar until it breaks apart!

play_smash_wait.message: Hold down on a bar to smash it.
play_smash_wait.hint: Press and hold on any bar until it breaks!

play_smash_confirm.message: You smashed it! That feels good, right? Smash the other one too so we can start fresh.

play_smash_second_wait.message: Smash the last bar to clear the screen.
play_smash_second_wait.hint: Hold down on the bar to smash it!

play_circle_intro.message: Now let's build with circles! Tap the empty space twice to add a circle.

play_add_circle_wait.message: Double-tap the empty space to add a circle.
play_add_circle_wait.hint: Tap the open area twice to create a circle!

play_add_circle_confirm.message: There is your circle! Now cut it into 3 slices and color 2 of them to build 2/3.

play_build_twothirds_wait.message: Build 2/3 on the circle. Cut into 3 slices and color 2.
play_build_twothirds_wait.hint: Double-tap to cut slices, then single-tap 2 slices to color them!

play_circle_equiv_setup.message: You built 2/3 with a circle! Now add another circle and make it equivalent to 2/3.

play_circle_equiv_instruct.message: Now cut and color this circle to make it equivalent to 2/3. Remember, the colored areas need to be the same size!

play_circle_equiv_wait.message: Build a fraction equivalent to 2/3 on the second circle.
play_circle_equiv_wait.hint: Try 4/6! Cut into 6 slices and color 4.

play_circle_equiv_celebrate.message: Amazing! Both circles have the same amount colored. You built equivalent fractions with circles! Now smash them both.

play_smash_circle_1_wait.message: Hold down on a circle to smash it.
play_smash_circle_1_wait.hint: Press and hold on a circle to break it!

play_smash_circle_2_wait.hint: Hold down to smash the last circle!

play_mix_intro.message: Here is the big challenge. Can you show the same fraction as a bar AND a circle at the same time?

play_mix_add_bar_wait.message: Start by adding a bar. Double-tap the empty space.
play_mix_add_bar_wait.hint: Tap the open area twice to add a bar!

play_mix_build_bar.message: Now build any fraction you want on the bar. You get to choose! How about 1/3?

play_mix_bar_wait.message: Build 1/3 on the bar. Cut into 3 pieces and color 1.
play_mix_bar_wait.hint: Double-tap to cut into 3 pieces, then tap 1 piece to color it!

play_mix_bar_confirm.message: You built 1/3 on a bar! Now add a circle and build the same amount on it.

play_mix_add_circle_wait.hint: Tap the open area twice to add a circle!

play_mix_circle_instruct.message: Now build a fraction equivalent to 1/3 on the circle. It could be 1/3, 2/6, or anything that shows the same amount!

play_mix_circle_wait.message: Build a fraction equivalent to 1/3 on the circle.
play_mix_circle_wait.hint: Try 2/6! Cut into 6 slices and color 2.

play_mix_celebrate.message: You did it! The bar and the circle both show the same amount. Equivalent fractions work on any shape!

play_mix_question.message: You showed the same fraction on a bar and a circle. How do you know they are equivalent?

options.label: The colored amounts are the same size

play_final_redirect.message: Good thinking! But the numbers do not have to be the same. 1/3 and 2/6 have different numbers. What matters is the colored amount.

play_final_retry.message: Equivalent fractions have the same colored amount, even if the numbers are different. Does that make sense?

play_final_give.message: Think about everything you built today. Every time the colored parts were the same size, the fractions were equivalent. The shape and the numbers can be different!

play_final_confirm.message: That is right! The shape does not matter. The numbers do not matter. What matters is the amount that is colored. You really understand equivalent fractions!

play_smash_finale.message: Now for the fun part. Smash everything on the screen!

play_smash_finale_wait.message: Hold down to smash! Clear the whole screen.
play_smash_finale_wait.hint: Hold down on each shape to smash it!

complete.message: You did it! You built fractions, found equivalents, and smashed them all. Remember, if the colored parts are the same size, the fractions are equivalent. Great job today!
